title: Retention policy fabric and replayable evidence manifest for interactive request artifacts
creator: Ariadne Park
description:
Problem: Customers need deterministic, auditable retention controls for prompts, responses, request logs, and derived metrics across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. The current system supports per-route TTLs and ad hoc exports, but lacks a single policy fabric that composes per-tenant, per-route, and system defaults into a clear effective retention, plus a reproducible evidence export that is cryptographically verifiable and replayable for audits.

Goal: Ship a retention policy fabric that: (1) computes and exposes the effective retention for any stored artifact (prompt, response, log, metric sample) taking into account route defaults, tenant overrides, and regulatory constraints; (2) surfaces the effective policy in Console and APIs; (3) produces replayable evidence manifests (signed bundles) suitable for legal/compliance review and forensic replay; (4) integrates with existing eviction/purge pipelines, regional residency metadata, and legal-hold workflows.

Scope: per-route/tenant retention profiles, retention inheritance rules, evidence manifest schema and exporter, Console UX surface for effective retention and replay instructions, backend tagging and S3 lifecycle markers, automated test harness for policy simulation and canary purges. This ticket focuses on the PM spec and acceptance criteria; design and engineering epics will be linked as sub-issues.
acceptance_criteria: Define a canonical effective-retention computation algorithm that accepts: route_profile, tenant_overrides, legal_hold_exceptions, region_residency_policy, and returns TTLs for prompts, responses, request_logs, metrics.
Console must display the computed effective retention for a route and ability to preview for a selected tenant and date range.
Add an API endpoint GET /v1/retention/effective?route={}&tenant={}&artifact_type={} that returns the effective policy (JSON schema) and proof-chain reference.

Implement an evidence manifest format (manifest.json + signature) that includes: list of object URIs, per-object retention metadata, provenance hashes, timestamped policy version, and a signature produced by KMS/HSM. Example manifest must be attached to exported bundle.

Evidence bundles produced via Console or API export should be verifiable offline (manifest signature verified with public key) and contain replay instructions (order, dependencies, original timestamps) so artifacts can be reconstructed for forensic review.

Eviction workers obey the computed effective TTL and skip objects under an active legal_hold; purged objects generate an audit entry and a final evidence snapshot if 'snapshot_on_purge' is configured.
A policy-simulation job can run against a sample tenant and produce a diff report describing what would be deleted and why.
Security review completed and sign-off documented before release to dedicated/private customers.
technical_notes: Effective retention algorithm: Evaluate in order: global policy -> region overrides -> tenant defaults -> route-level policy -> route-tenant overrides. Resolve conflicts: most-restrictive (longest retention) wins unless legal_hold present (override to preserve). For sampled metrics, include sampling window and retention multiplier metadata.

Evidence manifest schema v1: top-level keys: version, generated_at (ISO8601), policy_snapshot_id, exported_by, signature_scheme, signature, objects: [{uri, type, created_at, sha256, retention_policy_reference}], recorded_keys: [KMS_key_id], provenance_chain: [policy_ids]. Manifest must be small (max 2MB) and accompany the ZIP/TAR of artifacts.

Storage integration: tag objects with x-retention-policy-id and x-region-residency. S3 lifecycle rules can be derived from policy_id->lifecycle mapping for hosted deployments. For private deployments, provide a converter script and sample lifecycle config.
Purge worker changes: consult retention service for effective TTL; implement 'soft-delete' window (7 days by default) during which evidence snapshot can be produced and legal hold can be applied.

Replayable export: include per-object 'original_offset' and 'replay_order' to allow deterministic rehydration. For encrypted objects, include wrapped data keys and key IDs; do not include plaintext keys in the export.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (preview): deploy retention service behind feature-flag; compute effective retention read-only and surface in Console for selected beta tenants. Phase 2 (exports): enable evidence-manifest exporter for beta tenants; run manual exports and verify signatures. Phase 3 (enforcement): switch purge workers to consult retention service; run canary on non-production tenants for 48h. Phase 4 (rollout): opt-in for all hosted tenants, provide operator scripts for Dedicated/Private customers and migration checklist. Backfill: annotate existing objects with policy_id tags (batch job) and create a 'policy_snapshot' record at time of backfill for audit. Rollback: preserve objects during soft-delete window and restore tags from snapshot for any rollback within 7 days.
qa_strategy: Unit tests for retention computation with 100% branch coverage for conflict resolution logic
Integration tests that simulate cross-region eviction and legal hold scenarios (end-to-end)
Crypto verification tests to validate manifest signature generation and offline verification
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect effective retention leading to premature deletion. Mitigation: conservative default is longest retention; initial enforcement behind feature flag and canary runs.
Risk: Manifest signatures rely on KMS availability. Mitigation: fallback signer with recorded chain and durable storage of signed manifests; export retry on failure.
Risk: Large evidence export sizes. Mitigation: provide sampled exports and chunked bundle creation; include hashed pointers instead of full artifacts on initial export if requested.
acceptance_test_plan: Create a synthetic tenant with mixed route policies and a legal_hold on subset; run simulation and assert that simulation lists exact objects excluded from purge and those preserved by legal_hold.
Generate an evidence export for a 7-day window; verify manifest signature using public key and replay artifacts to a temp bucket; verify hash matches original objects.
Console preview: pick a route and tenant and confirm UI shows effective retention, underlying rule provenance (which policy contributed), and a link to export evidence for last 30 days.

notes: This PM ticket is intentionally focused on the policy fabric and evidence manifest contract. Engineering tickets should implement the retention-service (read/write), eviction worker integration, export worker, and migration / backfill jobs. Design tickets govern Console UX and export UX. Close coordination with Security and Compliance required for signature key management, regional constraints, and attestation language.
